patch.objective: Vulnerability types: application (memory injection, buffer overflow, race conditions with time-of-check (TOC) and time-of-use (TOU), malicious update), operating system (OS)-based, web-based (SQL injection (SQLi), cross-site scripting (XSS)), hardware (firmware, end-of-life, legacy), virtualization (VM escape, resource reuse), cloud-specific, supply chain, cryptographic, misconfiguration, mobile device (side loading, jailbreaking), zero-day

sources.cite: CompTIA Security+ (V7), exam SY0-701: domains General security concepts 12%, Threats, vulnerabilities, and mitigations 22%, Security architecture 18%, Security operations 28%, Security program management and oversight 20%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16 for this Security+ band. The page lists the five domains and weights above, says English SY0-701 retires on June 11, 2027, and describes the topics: resilience and recovery (high availability, site considerations, testing, power, platform diversity, backups, continuity of operations); third-party risk (vendor assessment, selection, agreements, monitoring, questionnaires, rules of engagement); network attacks among the malicious activities; alerting and monitoring. The objectives PDF was not re-read; the objective wording is the course seed's.

sources.cite: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series, SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.note: Read 2026-11-14 through a summarizing fetch. Relevant text: primary defenses are 'parameterized queries when including dynamic data in SQL requests' and mapping structural choices to 'a strict allow-list of fixed, application-owned values'; manual escaping is strongly discouraged; least privilege: never give application accounts DBA or admin rights, and grant access through views; 'Input validation complements parameter binding; it does not replace it.'
